hints: The pulling force $P$ acts at $30^\circ$ above the incline: its components are $P\cos 30^\circ$ parallel to the slope (upwards) and $P\sin 30^\circ$ perpendicular to the slope (upwards away from the plane).
Resolve perpendicular to the slope to find normal reaction: $R + P\sin 30^\circ = mg\cos 40^\circ \implies R = 1.2\cos 40^\circ - P\sin 30^\circ$.
At limiting equilibrium, friction is $F = \mu R = 0.32R$. For minimum $P$, impending motion is down the slope so friction acts up the slope: $P\cos 30^\circ + 0.32R = 1.2\sin 40^\circ$.
For maximum $P$, impending motion is up the slope so friction acts down the slope: $P\cos 30^\circ - 0.32R = 1.2\sin 40^\circ$. Solve both to get the interval $0.676 \le P \le 1.04$.
walkthrough:
Resolve forces perpendicular to the $40^\circ$ inclined plane to find the normal reaction $R$ in terms of $P$:
$$R + P\sin 30^\circ = mg\cos 40^\circ \implies R = 0.12(10)\cos 40^\circ - P\sin 30^\circ = 1.2\cos 40^\circ - 0.5P$$

Calculate the limiting friction magnitude $F = \mu R$ with $\mu = 0.32$:
$$F = 0.32(1.2\cos 40^\circ - 0.5P) = 0.384\cos 40^\circ - 0.16P$$

For the minimum force $P_{\min}$, the particle is on the point of sliding down the plane, so friction acts up the plane:
$$P\cos 30^\circ + F = mg\sin 40^\circ$$
$$P\cos 30^\circ + (0.384\cos 40^\circ - 0.16P) = 1.2\sin 40^\circ$$
$$P(\cos 30^\circ - 0.16) = 1.2\sin 40^\circ - 0.384\cos 40^\circ$$
$$P(0.866025 - 0.16) = 0.771345 - 0.294160 \implies 0.706025P = 0.477185$$
$$P_{\min} = \frac{0.477185}{0.706025} \approx 0.67587 \approx 0.676\text{ N}$$

For the maximum force $P_{\max}$, the particle is on the point of sliding up the plane, so friction acts down the plane:
$$P\cos 30^\circ - F = mg\sin 40^\circ$$
$$P\cos 30^\circ - (0.384\cos 40^\circ - 0.16P) = 1.2\sin 40^\circ$$
$$P(\cos 30^\circ + 0.16) = 1.2\sin 40^\circ + 0.384\cos 40^\circ$$
$$P(0.866025 + 0.16) = 0.771345 + 0.294160 \implies 1.026025P = 1.065505$$
$$P_{\max} = \frac{1.065505}{1.026025} \approx 1.03848 \approx 1.04\text{ N}$$

Combine both boundaries into the inequality for the permissible range of $P$:
$$0.676 \le P \le 1.04\text{ N}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Resolve forces perpendicular to the inclined plane: the component of $P$ pulling away from the plane is $P\sin 30^\circ$, the normal reaction is $R$, and the perpendicular component of weight is $mg\cos 40^\circ$:
$$R + P\sin 30^\circ = mg\cos 40^\circ$$
Substitute $m = 0.12\text{ kg}$ and $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$R = 1.2\cos 40^\circ - P\sin 30^\circ = 1.2\cos 40^\circ - 0.5P$$

Recall the limiting friction formula $F = \mu R$ with coefficient $\mu = 0.32$:
$$F = 0.32(1.2\cos 40^\circ - 0.5P) = 0.384\cos 40^\circ - 0.16P$$

Determine the downslope weight component acting parallel to the plane:
$$W_{\text{down}} = mg\sin 40^\circ = 1.2\sin 40^\circ$$

Find the minimum value of $P$ ($P_{\min}$). When $P$ is minimal, the particle is on the verge of sliding down, so friction acts up the slope:
$$P\cos 30^\circ + F = 1.2\sin 40^\circ$$

Find the maximum value of $P$ ($P_{\max}$). When $P$ is maximal, the particle is on the verge of sliding up, so friction acts down the slope:
$$P\cos 30^\circ - F = 1.2\sin 40^\circ$$
$$P\cos 30^\circ - (0.384\cos 40^\circ - 0.16P) = 1.2\sin 40^\circ$$
$$P(\cos 30^\circ + 0.16) = 1.2\sin 40^\circ + 0.384\cos 40^\circ$$

State the complete set of values of $P$ in equilibrium as a closed interval:
$$0.676 \le P \le 1.04\text{ N}$$
